dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 14.3-day, 2.3% dip repeating four times on a young spotted M dwarf with a flat bottom and no secondary or odd-even difference, consistent with a 5.1-Earth-radius planet. The star is highly variable and the dip depth changes by ~37% between sectors and between transits and the transit duration is longer than central, leaving spot contamination and measurement scatter as an alternative to a uniform-depth planet. One more year of TESS and ground-based transit photometry to measure depth stability are needed to rule out a variable-star blend and confirm the planet.

reasons.why: M dwarf is a strong variable spotted rotator (20749 ppm, 0.461 d) with high variability_chi2_dof 2.542 and phase_curve amplitude 3882 ppm ratio_to_depth 0.2052 chi2 22.88 dof 9; signal_over_rotation 31.094360086767896 is not a multiple, but variability can mimic transit shape at phase_curve chi2 excess. Per tool guidance this counts only with phase-curve swing or non-transit shape; V sigma -2.423 is flat-bottomed (b=0.1184) favouring transit, so variability argues for but does not prove a binary or blend.

reasons.why: Single-transit depths are highly inconsistent (p=0.000900) — sectors.p_constant 0.1452 shows 13727 vs 19910 ppm (36.76% change). Such sector changes plus strong spot modulation mean depth scatter and large phase_curve chi2 could arise from unocculted spots altering transit depth and out-of-transit baseline, mimicking a depth-change blend, rather than from multiple distinct blended events.
